seed.experience.1: Do not split the work into subtasks when there would be only ONE subtask: do that work yourself, within the current task. The exception is a well-grounded suspicion that the work will not fit into the input token limit — then splitting is justified.
seed.experience.2: The time/quality value of this task (printed in the assignment on a line of its own) decides ONE thing: whether you run the checks yourself. The rule: 0.00 — run no checks at all; otherwise run those whose degree of need is STRICTLY GREATER than one minus that value (1.00 — the threshold is 0, that is the whole suite; 0.50 — only a need above 0.50). A task that releases a version always has 1.00: no saving of time cancels the full run before a build is assembled. And remember the price: two full runs going at the same time take twice as long (2621 checks — 27 minutes alone against 53 minutes side by side), so start a run of your own only when it is really needed.
seed.experience.3: ALWAYS write the list of required checks into the report — both when you ran them yourself and when time/quality is zero and you ran nothing: the task that runs the suite for everybody builds its set out of these lists. Put the section FIRST in the report and in exactly this shape: the line «## Требуемые тесты» (a fixed marker, it is not translated), then one line per check — «- CheckName — 0.7». It goes first because your result reaches the neighbours truncated (about 4000 characters), and whatever is appended to the end of the report will not get there. Write the name that selects a run in this project (see the project experience for how exactly); nothing to check — say so in a line, but keep the section itself.
seed.experience.4: The degree of need of a check is a number from 0.0 to 1.0, and the higher it is, the more the check must be run: it is compared with the threshold computed from time/quality. Set it like this: 1.0 — checks written for the change itself and those that fail without it; 0.8 — checks of the same file, the same entity or the same mechanism that the change touches directly; 0.5 — sentinel checks against drift (record counters, the database schema number, dictionary contents) and neighbouring places with the same mechanism; 0.2 — what could be affected on the edge; 0.0 — unrelated to the change at all, do not list those. This is an estimate of the risk «will it break», not a wish «it would be nice to run».

orgs.join.hint: You are not a member of this organisation yet: it arrived on this server by replication and created no members here. When you switch, you become its member with the administrator role, and that record travels to the conductor at the next session.
orgs.joined: You are now a member of “{0}”
orgs.server.on: The server is part of the organisation: its data is replicated here. Clear the checkbox to disconnect it.
orgs.server.off: The server is not part of the organisation. Tick the checkbox to add it: the conductor hands it a code (S0, S1, …) and replication begins.
orgs.server.locked: The organisation's server list is maintained by its conductor. On this server only its own row can be changed.
orgs.servers.locked: The conductor of this organisation is another server, so only this computer's row can be changed here: disconnect it from the organisation or bring it back. Other servers and the choice of conductor are edited on the conductor.
orgs.conductor.is: Filled circle: this server is the conductor of the organisation. It alone starts tasks automatically and on schedule and hands out the server codes S0, S1, …
orgs.conductor.pick: Empty circle: this server is not the conductor. Select the circle to make it the conductor — the previous one loses the mark.
orgs.conductor.off: The server is not part of the organisation, so it cannot become the conductor: tick the checkbox on the left first.
orgs.conductor.locked: The conductor is appointed by the conductor itself. From this server the conductor role is handed over by a request in the “Servers” section, not here.
orgs.conductor.star: The star is the conductor's mark: it stands next to the server that is the conductor right now.
settings.serverMoved: The server address, port, folders of this computer and the server administrator password live on the «Servers» tab, in the local server form.
servers.title: Cluster servers
servers.hint: A server is an AI2P installation on a separate computer. Servers and organizations are linked many-to-many: one server serves several organizations, an organization lives on several servers. The local server always comes first. Joining a cluster is two-way: the request is confirmed by a person on the conductor.
servers.name: Server name
servers.hostnameHint: DNS name or IP the server is reached by in its own network: cluster peers see this address, and links are built from it until a second host name is set
servers.hostname2Hint: The address the server is seen by from OUTSIDE (public name or router IP with port forwarding): task and file links are built from it, and cluster neighbours call this server by it when its inner address is not visible from their network. Empty — there is no second address
servers.peerHostname2Hint: The second address of this server — the one it is seen by from outside its network. Normally it arrives from the server itself; type it by hand if there was no exchange yet. A call tries the addresses in turn: the first one, then this one
servers.port2Hint: port forwarded on the router; empty — the same port
servers.bindAddressHint: 0.0.0.0 — all interfaces (required for a cluster), 127.0.0.1 — this computer only; applied after restart
servers.local.title: Local server
servers.codeHint: Code of the local server in the current organization; it is part of task numbers (T-18-S1). Handed out by the conductor, not editable by hand.
servers.unidHint: servers recognize each other by it during replication; an address will not do — it changes
servers.orgs.empty: This server has no organizations yet
servers.check.other: A DIFFERENT server answers at this address (internal key does not match)
servers.savedRestart: Settings saved; the address and port are applied after restart
servers.open: Open this server (new tab): that is also where you change your password on it
servers.delete: Delete the server from the list
servers.deleteConfirm: Delete this server record? It is removed entirely, together with its organization links, and the code it was given (S1) is freed. This is allowed only while there has been no replication with it — that is how a failed first connection is cleaned up.
servers.delete.done: The server has been deleted from the list
servers.requests.all.hint: Also list requests that have been decided: accepted, rejected and withdrawn conductor change requests, and rejected server join requests. Without the box only servers and requests awaiting a decision are shown.
servers.request.title: Server join request
servers.request.hint: Another server asks to join an organization. Joining is two-way: the decision is yours — you are on the organization conductor.
servers.request.done.accept: The server has joined the organization
servers.request.done.defer: Request deferred — it stays in the server list
servers.request.done.reject: Request rejected; the journal entry remains
servers.join.title: Join an organization of this server
servers.join.hint: The request goes to the organization conductor and is confirmed by a person on that side. No email or password on that server is needed: the request is anonymous and signed by your account.
servers.join.orgCodeHint: May be left empty if that server has a single organization
servers.join.sent: Request sent — waiting for a decision on that server
servers.join.state.pending: Request is awaiting confirmation in the organization
task.server.readOnly: The task belongs to another server and is edited there
task.server.ownHint: Task of this server — editable here
task.server.dialogHint: A task has exactly one owning server: it is edited there and its jobs run there. The task number does not change.
task.server.warning: After the change the task becomes read-only on this server; it will be editable on the selected one.
task.server.dialogHint.template: A template also has exactly one owning server: it is edited there. The template moves together with its whole subtree of nodes; node numbers do not change.
task.server.warning.template: After the change the template and its nodes become read-only on this server; they will be editable on the selected one.
schedule.server.hint: A schedule fires on its own server; without a server it is run by the conductor
schedule.server.readOnly: Schedule of another server — edited there
executors.conductorOnly: Executors are edited on the organization conductor
projects.commonHint: A path INSIDE the project folder (for example media); its contents are replicated between servers, empty — not replicated
servers.takeover: Hand tasks over to the conductor
servers.takeover.confirm: Hand all tasks of this server over to the conductor? They become editable again, but here.
models.server.readOnly: The entry belongs to another server and is edited there
models.server.adminHint: A local model belongs to this server: only the server administrator can save changes (Servers tab -> server administrator login).
servers.request.applicantHint: "ACCEPT" also makes the applicant a member of the organization: their account is created here from the request — with the same key and the same password as on their server. Do not create the same person here by hand — in a cluster a person has a single account.
repl.title: Replication
repl.hint: Every server replicates with the conductor only. Empty means no automatic replication - by button only.
repl.pairHint: How often THIS server exchanges with the selected one. Empty means no automatic replication - by button only.
repl.intervalHint: at least 30 s; empty - manual only
repl.conductorOnly: Intervals of another server are set by the organization conductor
repl.diagnostics.hint: A cursor is a position in the change log: 'received' is how far we read the peer, 'sent' is how far the peer read us. Lag is how many of our changes it has not taken yet.
repl.none: No replication with this server: it is not connected to any of your organizations
repl.pending.hint: The database refused these rows. Replication is not held up by them and retries them every session. If the attempt count grows but the row never applies, press «Initial replication»: the queue is forgotten and the change log is re-read from scratch.
repl.conflicts.auto: A row changed on both servers needs no decision: the last-writer-wins rule applies. This is an all-time counter; it is cleared by the «Initial replication» button.
repl.reset.done: Cursors reset: the next session re-reads everything
repl.conflicts.title: File conflicts
repl.conflicts.hint: These files changed on BOTH servers within the replication interval and are therefore not replicated. The left version is the conductor's, the right one is the ordinary server's. A decision applies at the next replication and for one session only.
repl.resolve.left: Take the left one (the conductor's version)
repl.resolve.right: Take the right one (this server's version)
repl.resolve.rename_left: Rename the left one - both versions stay
repl.resolve.rename_right: Rename the right one - both versions stay
repl.resolve.saved: Decision saved; it applies at the next replication
repignore.title: Replication filter (.repignore)
repignore.hint: What NOT to replicate from the Common folder. Syntax as in .gitignore: # is a comment, cache/ is a directory, *.tmp is a mask, ! brings a file back, a leading / anchors to the folder root. An empty filter deletes the file.
repignore.notConfigured: The Common folder is not set on this server - the filter has nowhere to live. Fill it in above and save the project.
repl.resolve.new: Enter a new key - both versions are dropped
repl.resolve.applied: Decision applied; it reaches the other server at the next replication
models.keyOrgHint: The key belongs to the organization: it is encrypted with the organization key and replicated to its servers. The organization key itself is stored on this computer only (secrets.json) and never replicated.
models.keyNoOrgKey: This server has not received the organization key yet - there is nothing to store or read API keys with. The conductor issues it when it confirms the server joining the organization.
settings.runMode.hint: How this server was started. Console is the default. The makeAsServise script in the installation folder turns the application into an OS service (service name AI2P); the same script removes the service with the -Remove key. A service has no desktop, so it does not open the browser at startup.
settings.runMode.markOnly: the installation is marked as a service, but this run is a console one
settings.versionHint: Format 1.<build number>; the build number is the number of the task this version was built from. The install script compares versions by it, and on the first start after an update the application brings the data up to date.
models.doc.missing: There is no document for this model yet. It lives in the application documentation directory - put the file at the path below.
models.doc.otherLang: No translation into the interface language yet; showing the document in
setup.hint.lang: The remaining first-start screens and the application itself will speak this language. Your browser language is suggested; you can change it later in the settings.
setup.lang.hint: The list shows the installed dictionaries (i18n files). If your browser language is missing, English is suggested.
setup.dirs.hint: Folders of this computer: model weights, downloaded archives and installed packages (ComfyUI, llama.cpp). A relative path is resolved against the folder NEXT TO AI2P — an installation in C:\ai\AI2P puts the weights into C:\ai\models. A full path is accepted as well, for example on another drive.
setup.adminSame: The password is the same as the server administrator password
setup.adminSame.hint: The server has a separate local administrator sign-in that opens the settings of the computer itself: address, folders, model catalog. With this box ticked both passwords are the same, and you sign in as the user and as the server administrator at once. Clear it if the passwords must differ.
setup.hint.usage: What you are going to do most of the time. Based on the answer AI2P creates three AI executors on the most suitable models, builds a team out of them and you, and creates the first project.
setup.usage.hint: «No typical use» finishes the first start as before: the executors, the team and the project you create yourself in the application.
setup.usage.noModels: There are no ready-to-work models with such skills right now: a cloud model needs an API key, a local one needs to be installed. The team and the project will still be created; add AI executors later in «Settings → Models».
setup.hint.project: A project is a folder on the disk and everything around it: tasks, objects and files. Enter the name and the folder; the executors and the team AI2P creates itself.
setup.project.name: Project name
setup.project.dir.hint: A full path to the folder with the project files on this computer: it is created if it does not exist. Empty — the project has no files yet, the folder can be set later in its card.
setup.usage.created: Created: {0} executor(s), the «{1}» team, the «{2}» project.
join.toUi: Wait for the decision in the application
join.toUi.hint: The "Next" button takes you into the application: the decision on the request can be asked there too (the server list), and once the connection is confirmed the organization data shows up.
join.sameEmail: The conductor already knows a person with this e-mail, so the request was sent on their behalf and this server took over their account. After the connection is confirmed, sign in here with THE SAME password they have on the conductor: in a cluster a person has one account and one password.
join.sameEmail.stuck: The conductor already knows a person with this e-mail, but their account cannot be taken over here: this server already has organizations. Connect from a clean installation or use another e-mail.
ui.noOrg.title: This server is not connected to an organization yet
ui.noOrg.hint: The request awaits a decision on the conductor. Until it is confirmed there is no data here: the settings and the server list are available — the list is also where you ask for the decision and start replication manually.
ui.noOrg.disabled: Not available until the server is connected to an organization
join.sameEmail.setup: The conductor already knows a person with this e-mail. Send the request from the connection screen (/setup): there the server takes over their account and the request goes through.
join.sameEmail.ask: The conductor already knows a person with the e-mail "{1}" — {0}. An e-mail is the login here, so this is the same person. To connect on their behalf, prove it is you: enter their password on the conductor.
join.hint.sameEmail: The conductor already knows a person with this e-mail. The request can be sent on their behalf — prove it is you by entering their password on the conductor.
join.password: That person's password on the conductor
join.password.hint: This is the ordinary sign-in password ON THE CONDUCTOR — the one that opens the organization there. The conductor checks it itself; the password is not stored here. It also becomes the sign-in password for this server: in a cluster a person has one account and one password. If you do not know it, this is somebody else: go back to the "User" step and use another e-mail.
join.sameEmail.wrong: Wrong password. The password needed is the one this person signs in with on the conductor. If you do not know it, ask the organization owner, or go back to the "User" step and apply with another e-mail.
join.sameEmail.unset: The person with this e-mail has no password on the conductor, so there is no way to prove it is you. Set a password for them on the conductor (Settings → Users) and send the request again — or use another e-mail here.
servers.request.member.add: Create the executor — make the applicant a member of the organization
servers.request.member.hint: Membership in an organization IS a human executor bound to the applicant's account. Without one the person will never see the organization, no matter how many replication sessions run. The role given is the ordinary one (editor) and can be changed on the "Executors" tab.
servers.request.member.warn: The box is cleared: the server will be connected, but the applicant will NOT become a member of the organization — on their side they hit the "you are not a member of any organization" page and cannot work until you create an executor for them by hand.
servers.request.done.accept.noMember: The server has joined the organization; the applicant was NOT made a member
conductor.assignHint: Hand the conductor role over to this server. This is a separate operation: the request travels to the other side at the next replication session, and a person there makes the decision.
conductor.title: Changing the conductor of the organization
conductor.hint: An organization has exactly one conductor: it issues server codes, maintains the catalogs and everyone else replicates with it. That is why the conductor role is not switched by a checkbox — one side files a request, and a person on the other side accepts or rejects it.
conductor.noteHint: It will be read by whoever makes the decision on the other side
conductor.sendHint: The request travels to the other side at the next replication session. Until it is decided the conductor does not change, and you can withdraw your request right here.
conductor.sent: The conductor change request has been filed
conductor.takeover.ready: The conductor has not responded within 12 hours: the request may be accepted unilaterally — this server will become the conductor on its own.
conductor.takeover.wait: If the conductor does not respond, the request may be accepted unilaterally in
conductor.otherSide: The decision on this request is made on the other side — here it is read-only.
conductor.done.accepted: The request is accepted: the conductor has changed

prompt.cli.40:
AI2P ACTIONS CAN BE CALLED AS A COMMAND, NOT ONLY WITH A MARKER. A command line client is available next to you:

    {0} help

It calls the API of this very server on behalf of YOUR JOB (the address and the token are already in the environment variables {1} and {2}), so the answer arrives AT ONCE, within your same turn, and it has no limit on the number of requests. A marker, on the contrary, ends your turn: the system executes it and starts you again with the whole context — that is expensive. So prefer the command and keep markers for the cases where the command is not available.

Common commands:
    {0} help                       all actions available to this job
    {0} parent                     the parent task
    {0} siblings                   sibling tasks
    {0} children T-22              subtasks of a task (no code — your own)
    {0} task T-15                  a task by its code
    {0} chat T-15                  the chat of a task
    {0} find «part of the title»   search for tasks
    {0} message --text "..."       write to a human in the task chat
    {0} status T-15 --status pending --restart     send another task back to work
    {0} subtask --title "..." --description-file d.md   create a subtask
    {0} experience --text "..." --scope project        record experience
    {0} file <link>                fetch a file of the task onto the disk

Long texts are easier to pass in a file: every parameter has the form «--name-file <path>», and the whole arguments object can be given as ready JSON on the standard input («{0} call create_task --stdin»). Every call goes through the security rules of the task: a forbidden action returns a clear refusal and exit code 1. A question to a human (AI2P_QUESTION) and a letter to a neighbour with waiting for the answer stay MARKERS: that is not a call but a pause of the job for hours, and a synchronous command would not live that long.

prompt.flow.1:
## Condition task
Your job is to decide from the task description and chat whether the condition holds, and to return the decision STRICTLY as true or false. Report it with the set_condition_result action, parameter value (true — the "Yes" branch, false — the "No" branch); an agent without AI2P tools uses the command "ai2p condition true" / "ai2p condition false" or a marker on its own line: AI2P_CONDITION: {"value": true}. There is no third outcome: if you cannot decide unambiguously, ask the human instead of guessing. Without a decision the system will not pick a branch, and the hierarchy run stops. The system applies the branch when you finish: the branch not taken is cancelled automatically, you need neither cancel it nor start the chosen one. Branches:
prompt.flow.3: - Branch "{0}": no task, "create tasks" is set — if you choose this branch, create its tasks as subtasks of this task BEFORE finishing: create_task (marker AI2P_SUBTASK) or create_tasks_from_template with a template node code (command "ai2p from-template T-N", marker AI2P_FROM_TEMPLATE: {"template": "T-N"}).
prompt.flow.4: - Branch "{0}": no task — the hierarchy run ends on it.
prompt.flow.5: - Branch "{0}": no task — nothing is done, the hierarchy continues.
prompt.flow.8:
## Task of type {0}
This is a loop analyzer. Your job is to check the loop conditions from the task description, chat and the results of subtasks from previous passes, and to answer STRICTLY true or false: whether to make another pass. Answer with the set_loop_result action, parameter continue (true — conditions are met, another pass; false — exit the loop); an agent without AI2P tools uses the command "ai2p loop true" / "ai2p loop false" or a marker on its own line: AI2P_LOOP: {"continue": false}. There is no third outcome: if you cannot decide unambiguously, ask the human. Without an answer the system will not continue the loop, and the hierarchy run stops. The subtasks (loop body) are started and restarted by the system — do not start them yourself.
